answer: Because the derivation is a one-way function of the gale seed, the harbor timing is verifiable from the anchor record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. A farm that wants 163 keys as a result pays 163 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 410 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is trivial once and expensive in bulk. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
